summary.text: A mesoscale eddy is a swirl of ocean water roughly 10 to 500 km across that lasts from days to months.
Its currents circle around its centre, and the water inside usually has a different temperature and salinity from the sea around it.
Because they carry unusually warm or cold water as they move, these eddies help shift heat toward the poles and shape heat transport in parts of the ocean.

facts.label: Seen in
facts.value: Gulf Stream, Agulhas, Kuroshio, Antarctic Circumpolar Current

items.prompt: A satellite tracks a swirl of seawater about 200 km wide that keeps turning for several weeks. What would an oceanographer call it?

options.label: A Rossby wave
A mesoscale eddy
A tiny turbulent vortex
A tidal bore

items.explain: Swirls roughly 10 to 500 km across that last days to months are what oceanographers call mesoscale eddies.

items.prompt: Researchers find an ocean eddy whose core is clearly colder than the water around it. Which way is it most likely turning?

options.label: Anticyclonically
It is not turning
Cyclonically
Switching back and forth

items.explain: An eddy's water properties are tied to its spin: warm eddies turn anticyclonically and cold eddies turn cyclonically.

items.prompt: A research ship sails from open water into the middle of an ocean eddy and samples the water there. What does it usually find?

options.label: Water identical to the sea it just left
Water with no measurable current
Water that is only different at night
Water with its own temperature and saltiness

items.explain: Eddies are usually made of a different water mass, so their temperature and salinity differ from the water outside.

items.prompt: Large eddies keep appearing along strong currents such as the Gulf Stream. How do many of them form?

options.label: Passing ships stir the current into loops
Tides drag the water into circles
The current meanders and its bends break off
Undersea volcanoes heat the water into spirals

items.explain: An unstable current meanders and throws off eddies, much as a winding river cuts off an oxbow lake.

items.prompt: Why do navies and shipping companies keep an eye on where ocean eddies are?

options.label: They create giant waves on the surface
They block ships' radio signals
They pull ships down into whirlpools
They can have strong circulating currents

items.explain: Eddies may carry a vigorous circulation, which makes them a concern for naval and commercial operations at sea.

items.prompt: An eddy breaks away from a warm current and drifts toward the pole. What does this do to the ocean's heat?

options.label: It carries heat toward the pole
It carries heat toward the equator
It has no effect on where heat goes
It destroys the heat it holds

items.explain: Eddies move their unusually warm or cold water with them, and mesoscale eddies play a key role in moving heat poleward.
